data.hypothesis: The selected parent (5742ad4218cf4186) runs serial whenever the full requested team would average fewer than 256 options per worker. Instead, cap the static OpenMP team to the number of 256-option work grains available, using the serial path only when that yields fewer than two workers. This tests whether partial use of the passed thread budget can parallelize medium workloads without idle workers, while preserving the existing generic grain and complete output coverage. Prior aggregate OpenMP means are close; no gain is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: OpenMP grain and team-size choices for this Black-Scholes entrypoint.
memory_lessons.claim: The supplied baseline reports 7.529 ms, while five correct OpenMP variants report aggregate means from about 1.401 to 1.450 ms. The variants differ in grain/cutoff, but the reported aggregate results do not establish a per-size crossover or a reliably best threshold.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the partial-team cap against the selected parent's all-or-nothing serial cutoff across valid sizes and thread budgets, including region overhead near the crossover; retain it only if results support the generic policy.

data.notes: The supplied selected parent is correct with mean 0.001407827 s; the best reported prior T1 candidate is 0.001400686 s, and the reported 1024-options-per-worker variant is 0.001450097 s. The baseline mean is 0.007528638 s. Prior correctness logs report eight successful cases across varied seeds/patterns, with guards intact and inputs unchanged. These are historical controller measurements, not measurements of this candidate; no per-size crossover comparison is available here. This candidate retains the 256-option grain but allows a smaller bounded team where the parent falls back to serial. The controller should measure its overhead and gain and verify correctness/output coverage.
transformations: Kept the serial path for nonpositive n, one-thread budgets, and work insufficient for at least two 256-option grains.
Set the OpenMP team size to min(threads, n / 256), allowing partial use of the passed budget instead of switching directly from the full team to serial.
Retained static scheduling, a team no larger than the passed thread budget, and one distinct output write per loop iteration.
